text.p: Base metals meandered to generally steadier closes during featureless Wednesday afternoon trading on the LME, with an inconclusive trend in copper setting the tone for the whole complex, traders said.
"It has been pretty quiet most of the day. The trouble is that copper is in a terrible range at the moment," one said.

An early thrust towards $2,280 was repulsed yet again, and this left the copper market in a limbo, with the dip meeting expected support around $2,255. For most of the session trade was in a tight $2,255/65 band, with last business at $2,262, up $7.
"While it is like that, it is a licence to lose money," the trader said.
Meanwhile, the spread structure continued to ratchet outwards, with the overall cash/threes backwardation out to $250 by the close, against Tuesday's $238.
The tight period is end-Jan/early-Feb, and believed to represent major short positions held by a U.S. investment house and a Far Eastern trader, dealers said
On the LME Jan 29/31 was trading at $26 backwardation, February 18/19 was indicated at $6 premium, while, further forward, March/one day was at a $4/5 backwardation.

Aluminium was unable to build on some trade buying, against a background of rising physical premiums and a lack of Russian metal in Europe. However, the $1,625 break-out point on the charts was defended, and prices finished at $1,630, up $12.
Nickel prices edged away from early lows during late kerb trading, helped by some modest covering and copper gravitating higher, although trade was routine.
Despite the late uptick, prices struggled to regain $7,300 and last business was at $7,280, still down $20 from yesterday.

Zinc encountered difficulty in challenging Tuesday's 23-month peaks, but managed to hold the $1,150 level after a late flurry of local buying, well above initial lows. By the end of the kerb prices were at $1,150, up $12, and seen extending gains.
The lead market tried to push higher, but was restrained by a slow narrow band, with the important overhead target put around $720/725. Last trade was at an unchanged $713.
Tin similarly held in a tight range, with modest price dips supported at the $6,000 level. Prices finished a lacklustre day at $6,020, little changed from yesterday's $6,015 close.
The alloy market was marked lower with primary values, although trade was low-key. Three months closed at $1,525/30, down some $10.
